url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
Sure! Below is a complete, ready‑to‑use **Startup Statistics API** specification.  
It covers everything from the endpoint structure, query parameters, authentication, pagination, to example responses and error handling.

---

## 📦 API Overview

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Base URL** | `https://api.startupstats.com/v1` |
| **Authentication** | API Key (Bearer token) |
| **Rate Limiting** | 100 requests per minute (IP‑based) |
| **Versioning** | Semantic (`v1`, `v2`, …) |
| **Response Format** | JSON (default) |
| **Error Codes** | 400, 401, 403, 404, 429, 500 |

---

## 🔑 Authentication

All requests must include an `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```

> **Tip:** Store your API key securely (e.g., environment variables, secrets manager).

---

## 📁 Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/startups` | List startups with optional filters |
| `GET` | `/startups/{id}` | Retrieve a single startup by ID |
| `GET` | `/industries` | List all supported industries |
| `GET` | `/locations` | List all supported locations (countries, cities) |

> **Note:** All endpoints support `Accept: application/json`.

---

## 📦 Request Parameters

### 1. `GET /startups`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `page` | integer | No | Page number (default: 1) |
| `per_page` | integer | No | Items per page (default: 20, max: 100) |
| `sort_by` | string | No | Field to sort by (`name`, `valuation`, `funding`, `employees`) |
| `order` | string | No | `asc` or `desc` (default: `asc`) |
| `industry` | string | No | Filter by industry slug |
| `country` | string | No | Filter by country code (ISO 3166‑1 alpha‑2) |
| `city` | string | No | Filter by city name |
| `min_funding` | number | No | Minimum total funding (USD) |
| `max_funding` | number | No | Maximum total funding (USD) |
| `min_valuation` | number | No | Minimum valuation (USD) |
| `max_valuation` | number | No | Maximum valuation (USD) |
| `founding_year` | integer | No | Filter by founding year |
| `search` | string | No | Full‑text search on name, tagline, description |

> **Example:**  
> `GET https://api.startupstats.com/v1/startups?industry=fintech&country=US&page=2&per_page=10`

### 2. `GET /startups/{id}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Yes | UUID of the startup |

---

## 📄 Response Schema

### 1. List Response (`GET /startups`)

```json
{
  "meta": {
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 20,
    "total_pages": 5,
    "total_items": 100,
    "next_page": "https://api.startupstats.com/v1/startups?page=2&per_page=20",
    "prev_page": null
  },
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "c3a1f9b2-4d8e-4f3a-9b7c-1e2f3a4b5c6d",
      "name": "FinTech Innovators",
      "tagline": "Revolutionizing payments",
      "description": "A fintech startup focused on seamless cross‑border payments.",
      "industry": "fintech",
      "location": {
        "country": "US",
        "city": "San Francisco"
      },
      "founding_date": "2018-04-12",
      "employees": 45,
      "funding": {
        "total": 12000000,
        "rounds": [
          {
            "type": "Series A",
            "amount": 8000000,
            "date": "2020-07-01"
          },
          {
            "type": "Seed",
            "amount": 4000000,
            "date": "2019-02-15"
          }
        ]
      },
      "valuation": 50000000,
      "website": "https://fintechinnovators.com",
      "logo_url": "https://cdn.startupstats.com/logos/c3a1f9b2.png",
      "social_links": {
        "twitter": "https://twitter.com/fintechinnovators",
        "linkedin": "https://linkedin.com/company/fintechinnovators"
      }
    },
    ...
  ]
}
```

### 2. Single Startup (`GET /startups/{id}`)

Same structure as an individual item in the list response.

### 3. Industries (`GET /industries`)

```json
{
  "data": [
    { "slug": "fintech", "name": "Financial Technology" },
    { "slug": "healthtech", "name": "Health Technology" },
    { "slug": "edtech", "name": "Education Technology" },
    ...
  ]
}
```

### 4. Locations (`GET /locations`)

```json
{
  "countries": [
    { "code": "US", "name": "United States" },
    { "code": "GB", "name": "United Kingdom" },
    ...
  ],
  "cities": [
    { "name": "San Francisco", "country_code": "US" },
    { "name": "London", "country_code": "GB" },
    ...
  ]
}
```

---

## ⚠️ Error Handling

| Status Code | Error Code | Message | Example Response |
|-------------|------------|---------|------------------|
| `400` | `INVALID_PARAMETER` | One or more query parameters are invalid. | `{"error":"INVALID_PARAMETER","message":"per_page must be <= 100"}` |
| `401` | `UNAUTHORIZED` | Missing or invalid API key. | `{"error":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"API key missing or invalid."}` |
| `403` | `FORBIDDEN` | API key does not have permission. | `{"error":"FORBIDDEN","message":"Access denied."}` |
| `404` | `NOT_FOUND` | Resource not found. | `{"error":"NOT_FOUND","message":"Startup not found."}` |
| `429` | `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | Too many requests. | `{"error":"RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED","message":"Rate limit exceeded. Try again in 30 seconds."}` |
| `500` | `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` | Unexpected server error. | `{"error":"INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR","message":"An unexpected error occurred."}` |

> **Tip:** All error responses include a `retry_after` field (in seconds) when applicable.

---

## 🛠️ Example Usage

### 1. Using `curl`

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
     "https://api.startupstats.com/v1/startups?industry=fintech&country=US&page=1&per_page=10"
```

### 2. Using JavaScript (Fetch API)

```js
const apiKey = 'YOUR_API_KEY';
const url = 'https://api.startupstats.com/v1/startups?industry=fintech&country=US';

fetch(url, {
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
    'Accept': 'application/json'
  }
})
  .then(res => {
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
    return res.json();
  })
  .then(data => console.log(data))
  .catch(err => console.error(err));
```

### 3. Using Python (`requests`)

```python
import requests

API_KEY = 'YOUR_API_KEY'
BASE_URL = 'https://api.startupstats.com/v1'

headers = {
    'Authorization': f'Bearer {API_KEY}',
    'Accept': 'application/json'
}

params = {
    'industry': 'fintech',
    'country': 'US',
    'page': 1,
    'per_page': 10
}

response = requests.get(f'{BASE_URL}/startups', headers=headers, params=params)

if response.status_code == 200:
    data = response.json()
    print(data)
else:
    print(f'Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}')
```

---

## 📚 SDKs & Libraries

| Language | Package |
|----------|---------|
| JavaScript | `npm install @startupstats/sdk` |
| Python | `pip install startupstats-sdk` |
| Ruby | `gem install startupstats-sdk` |
| Java | `mvn dependency:copy -Dartifact=com.startupstats.sdk:startupstats-sdk:1.0.0` |

> **Tip:** Check the official GitHub repo for the latest SDK releases and examples.

---

## 📊 Monitoring & Analytics

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Dashboard** | Real‑time API usage dashboard (available in the developer portal). |
| **Metrics** | Request latency, error rates, throughput. |
| **Alerts** | Email/SMS alerts for rate limit breaches or 5xx errors. |
| **Logs** | Full request/response logs (retained for 30 days). |

---

## 📜 Changelog

| Version | Date | Changes |
|---------|------|---------|
| `v1.0.0` | 2024‑01‑15 | Initial release |
| `v1.1.0` | 2024‑03‑22 | Added `search` parameter, improved pagination |
| `v1.2.0` | 2024‑06‑10 | Added `min_funding`/`max_funding` filters, updated error codes |
| `v1.3.0` | 2024‑09‑05 | Added `founding_year` filter, updated SDKs |

---

## 🚀 Next Steps

1. **Get your API key** – Sign up at the developer portal.  
2. **Explore the sandbox** – Use the sandbox environment (`sandbox.api.startupstats.com`) for testing.  
3. **Integrate** – Add the API to your application using one of the SDKs or raw HTTP calls.  
4. **Monitor** – Keep an eye on usage and performance via the dashboard.  

---

### 🎉 Happy coding!  
If you run into any issues or have feature requests, feel free to open an issue on our GitHub repo or contact support at `support@startupstats.com`.
